message.content:
### Quick‑Start Checklist

| Step | What to Do | Why It Matters |
|------|------------|----------------|
| 1️⃣ | **Clean & Inspect** | A tidy, well‑maintained guitar looks more appealing and shows you care. |
| 2️⃣ | **Research Value** | Know the fair market price so you can price competitively. |
| 3️⃣ | **Take Quality Photos** | Clear, well‑lit shots of the body, neck, headstock, and any flaws build trust. |
| 4️⃣ | **Write a Detailed Description** | Include brand, model, year, condition, any upgrades, and why you’re selling. |
| 5️⃣ | **Choose Your Platform(s)** | Pick the right mix of online and local venues. |
| 6️⃣ | **Set a Realistic Price** | Price it slightly above your target to leave room for negotiation. |
| 7️⃣ | **Decide on Shipping or Local Pickup** | Shipping adds cost; local pickup saves money but requires safety precautions. |
| 8️⃣ | **Secure Payment** | Use secure methods (PayPal, Venmo, cash, or bank transfer). |
| 9️⃣ | **Close the Sale** | Confirm details, ship or hand over, and keep records for tax purposes. |

---

## 1. Clean & Inspect

- **Wash the body** with a damp cloth (avoid harsh chemicals).
- **Check the neck** for warping, loose frets, or missing fret markers.
- **Inspect hardware** (tuners, bridge, strap buttons) for rust or damage.
- **Test play** to ensure no buzzing or dead spots.
- **Document any imperfections** (scratches, dents, cracks) – honesty builds buyer confidence.

## 2. Research Value

| Source | How to Use |
|--------|------------|
| **Reverb.com** | Search “acoustic guitar” + brand/model/year. |
| **eBay Completed Listings** | Filter by “Sold” to see what buyers actually paid. |
| **Craigslist/Local Classifieds** | Look at recent sales in your area. |
| **Music Store Trade‑In Guides** | Some stores publish resale values. |
| **Forums (e.g., Gearslutz, Reddit r/guitar)** | Ask for opinions on similar instruments. |

**Tip:** If your guitar has upgrades (e.g., better pickups, custom finish), factor those into the price.

## 3. Take Quality Photos

- **Lighting:** Natural light works best; avoid harsh shadows.
- **Angles:** Front, back, side, headstock, neck, bridge, and any unique features.
- **Close‑ups:** Show any scratches, dents, or hardware details.
- **Context:** If you have a case or stand, include it to show the whole package.

## 4. Write a Detailed Description

- **Header:** “Acoustic Guitar – [Brand] [Model] – [Year] – Excellent Condition”
- **Body:**
  - Brand, model, year, serial number (if known).
  - Body wood type, neck wood, fretboard material.
  - Hardware details (tuners, bridge type, strap buttons).
  - Condition notes (e.g., “no cracks, minor scuffs on the back”).
  - Upgrades or modifications.
  - Reason for selling (“Upgrading to a new model”).
  - Any included accessories (case, strap, picks, tuner).
- **Call to Action:** “Contact me for more info or to arrange a viewing.”

## 5. Choose Your Platform(s)

| Platform | Best For | Pros | Cons |
|----------|----------|------|------|
| **Reverb.com** | Musicians, collectors | Large audience, built‑in payment, shipping tools | Listing fees, competition |
| **eBay** | General market | Auction or fixed price, buyer protection | Fees, shipping logistics |
| **Craigslist** | Local buyers | No fees, quick sale | Safety concerns, limited reach |
| **Facebook Marketplace** | Local & friends | Free, easy sharing | Limited buyer protection |
| **Local Music Stores** | Trade‑in or consignment | Immediate cash, no shipping | Lower price, limited inventory |
| **Nextdoor** | Neighborhood | Trust, local | Small audience |

**Strategy:** List on at least two platforms (e.g., Reverb + Craigslist) to maximize exposure. Use a consistent title and description across all sites.

## 6. Set a Realistic Price

- **Start high**: Price 10–15% above your target to allow room for negotiation.
- **Consider depreciation**: Acoustic guitars typically lose 20–30% in the first year.
- **Factor in upgrades**: If you added premium pickups or a custom finish, add $50–$200.
- **Check local comps**: If local listings show $300–$350 for similar models, aim for $320–$340.

## 7. Decide on Shipping or Local Pickup

| Option | When to Choose | Tips |
|--------|----------------|------|
| **Local Pickup** | You’re comfortable meeting strangers | Meet in a public place, bring a friend, use a lockbox if possible |
| **Shipping** | Buyer is far away or you’re in a different city | Use a sturdy case, insure the package, ship via tracked service |

**Shipping Costs:** Estimate $30–$50 for a standard case. Factor this into your price or ask the buyer to cover it.

## 8. Secure Payment

| Method | Pros | Cons |
|--------|------|------|
| **Cash** | Immediate, no fees | Risk of counterfeit, no buyer protection |
| **PayPal** | Secure, buyer/seller protection | Fees (~3% + $0.30) |
| **Venmo** | Instant, no fees | No buyer protection |
| **Bank Transfer** | No fees | Requires trust, no buyer protection |
| **Escrow Services** | Protects both parties | Fees, slower process |

**Recommendation:** For online sales, use PayPal or a reputable escrow service. For local sales, cash or Venmo is fine, but always verify authenticity.

## 9. Close the Sale

1. **Confirm details**: Date, time, location, payment method, shipping address.
2. **Get a receipt**: Print or email a simple receipt with the sale price and date.
3. **Ship or hand over**: If shipping, package securely and provide tracking. If local, hand over the instrument and collect payment.
4. **Keep records**: Save emails, screenshots, and receipts for tax purposes.

---

## Extra Tips & Common Pitfalls

| Tip | Why It Helps |
|-----|--------------|
| **Offer a “try before you buy”** | Builds buyer confidence. |
| **Be responsive** | Quick replies increase chances of sale. |
| **Avoid over‑promising** | Don’t claim “like new” if there are visible scratches. |
| **Use a lockbox** | Protects against theft during pickup. |
| **Check local regulations** | Some areas require a sales tax or license for large sales. |
| **Don’t rush** | Patience can lead to a better price. |

---

### Final Thought

Selling an acoustic guitar is largely about presentation and transparency. By cleaning it, photographing it well, pricing it right, and choosing the right platforms, you’ll attract serious buyers and get the best return on your instrument. Good luck, and enjoy the next chapter of your musical journey!
